saints.name: St. Sharbel Makhlūf
saints.title: Priest and Hermit
saints.shortBlurb: A Lebanese Maronite monk who lived hidden as a hermit and became a wonder of grace…
biography: Youssef Antoun Makhlouf was born on 8 May 1828 at Bekaa Kafra, the highest village in Lebanon, son of a mule driver who died when the boy was three. Raised in a devout home, he tended the family herd, praying hours in a grotto before an icon of the Virgin.

In 1851 he left home for the Lebanese Maronite Order, taking the name Sharbel after a second-century martyr of Antioch. Professed in 1853, he studied at Kfifan under Nimatullah Kassab, himself later a saint, and was ordained priest at Bkerke on 23 July 1859, returning to the monastery of Annaya.

In 1875 he withdrew to the monastery's hermitage of Saints Peter and Paul, where for twenty-three years he kept silence, fasting, and vigil before the Blessed Sacrament. Stricken while celebrating the Divine Liturgy on 16 December 1898, he died on Christmas Eve, aged seventy, and was buried on Christmas Day.

A light was seen over his tomb, and his body, long found incorrupt, drew pilgrims of every faith. Beatified by Paul VI in 1965 at the close of Vatican II and canonized in 1977, the 'Miracle Monk of Lebanon' is patron of Lebanon.
saints.knownFor: His hidden hermit's life and the miracles reported at his tomb.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Sharbel Makhlūf (vatican.va)
